title: Signal
description: One real, dated, published item found by the Scout and passed by the Verifier. The signal as a whole is real, so its provenance carries the external source. The summary and relevance note are written by the pipeline and carry their own labels. A Signal does not name its trends: the Trend holds the link (Trend.signalIds), and the UI derives the signal-to-trend links by inverting it. Shipped in data/signals.js as an array.

title.description: The source's own headline, which may stay in the source language.

sourceLanguage.description: Two-letter language code of the source (en, de). Used for the lang attribute on the title and quote, and to record German-language coverage (NF6).

summary.description: English paraphrase of what the source says. Written by the Scout.

quote.description: Optional short verbatim quote from the source. Length capped by QUOTE_MAX_WORDS (Q-4), checked in the M3 unit test, not here, because the cap is not yet set.

relevanceNote.description: Why this signal concerns Tracewell, lens-neutral and without any level of relevance (F2 precondition 4).

windowNote.description: Present only when the source falls outside the scanning brief's time window, saying so plainly.

label.description: Signals are real by invariant; the label is fixed.
